purpose: REGF3 version of grid A: the same network, operating points and events, with the REGF3 unit (dVOC) in the slot. The held-out device: tested once, for the poster, never in an RSI loop. Training grid: Kundur two-area with the device in generator 3's slot, recorded the way an operator would have it (ambient PMU recordings, staged voltage-reference steps, natural events) at three operating points, one after a topology change. Noisy, internal angle removed. sandbox_data/ goes to the solver; holdout/ has the clean runs, case.json and the answer key.

case.name: grid_A3
case.description: Kundur two-area (kundur_full.xlsx); device replaces GENROU 3 (bus 3); 150 MW of the bus-8 load moved to a new load PQ_2 at bus 10; area 1 re-dispatched (GENROU 2 at 400 MW, bus-7 load -300 MW) as in the medium case so a generator trip stays in limits; device REGF3

device_under_test.params_note: ANDES inputs. The six REGF1 parameters drawn the way REGF1's and REGF2's were (ANDES defaults scaled by numpy default_rng(seed).uniform(0.7, 1.3, 6) in the order wdrp, Qdrp, Tpm, KPplim, KIplim, Tr; wdrp and Qdrp times Sb/Sn), with seed 2, so the three units share no numbers; KPv = 6 as for the other two. REGF3 (dVOC) has no parameters of its own: its dVOC gain Kdvoc is a constant ANDES computes from wdrp and Qdrp (about 1.6e-10 here), and Qdrp enters only through it. The same device sits in grids A3, B3 and M3.

operating_conditions_log.op1: Normal topology. Device dispatched near 700 MW, voltage schedule 1.00 pu.
operating_conditions_log.op2: Normal topology. Device re-dispatched near 450 MW, voltage schedule 1.01 pu; the generator at bus 4 picks up the difference.
operating_conditions_log.op3: One circuit of the double line between buses 9 and 10 out of service for maintenance; bus-8 load about 100 MW heavier.

design_notes: Grid A with REGF3 instead of REGF1 (Nov 15), so the held-out device is tested on the grids the two training devices were tuned on and only the device differs. Grid M's dispatch and schedule were chosen for REGF1's damping; they have not been re-checked for REGF3.

Under REGF3 the staged voltage-reference steps barely move the unit: ANDES's dVOC gain Kdvoc is about 1e-10, so Vset enters its equations almost not at all, and in steady state the unit holds Q (no Q-V droop). The steps are kept so the events match grids A and A2 exactly.
Area 1 is re-dispatched as in the medium case (generator 2 at 400 MW, bus-7 load 300 MW lighter) so a generator trip stays within limits.

Every training and validation run with an event also has light ambient load variation (0.3% rms) underneath; the two ambient-only runs vary 1% rms. The two holdout runs are clean and never reach the solver.
